contents.text:
Use sql_file_index for simple filtered row scans when shard-local semantics are
acceptable. Prefer views over base tables:
- vrpentries: best default for file rows with directory context.
- pentries: file metadata with parent inode fields; use path() when you need a path.
- vrsummary and summary-family views: directory-level metadata.
- entries: low-level base table; avoid it for routine path questions.

Before writing SQL, inspect gufi://schemas/all and then the specific schema,
for example gufi://schemas/vrpentries.

Important semantics:
- ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions in sql_file_index
  apply per GUFI subtree, not globally across the whole index.
- For globally correct totals, grouping, or top-N ordering, use
  aggregate_sql_query and read gufi://aggregate-guide.
- Do not SELECT path FROM entries; entries has no path column.

usage: gufi_find [--help] [-v] [-maxdepth levels] [-mindepth levels] [-amin n]
                 [-anewer file] [-atime n] [-cmin n] [-cnewer file] [-ctime n]
                 [-empty] [-executable] [-false] [-gid n] [-group gname]
                 [-iname pattern] [-inum n] [-iregex pattern] [-links n]
                 [-lname pattern] [-mmin n] [-mtime n] [-name pattern]
                 [-newer file] [-path pattern] [-perm mode] [-readable]
                 [-regex pattern] [-samefile name] [-size n] [-true] [-type c]
                 [-uid n] [-user uname] [-writable] [-fprint file | -ls |
                 -print | -print0 | -printf format] [--num-results n]
                 [--smallest | --largest] [--compress] [--delim c]
                 [--skip-file filename] [-V]

GUFI version of find

options:
  --help                show this help message and exit
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  -maxdepth levels      Descend at most levels (a non-negative integer) levels of directories below the command line arguments. -maxdepth 0 means only apply the tests and actions to the command line arguments.
  -mindepth levels      Do not apply any tests or actions at levels less than levels (a non-negative integer). -mindepth 1 means process all files except the command line arguments.
  -amin n               File was last accessed n minutes ago.
  -anewer file          File was last accessed more recently than file was modified.
  -atime n              File was last accessed n*24 hours ago.
  -cmin n               File's status was last changed n minutes ago.
  -cnewer file          File's status was last changed more recently than file was modified.
  -ctime n              File's status was last changed n*24 hours ago.
  -empty                File is empty and is either a regular file or a directory.
  -executable           Matches files which are executable and directories which are searchable (in a file name resolution sense).
  -false                File is false and is either a regular file or a directory.
  -gid n                File's numeric group ID is n.
  -group gname          File belongs to group gname (numeric group ID allowed).
  -iname pattern        Like -name, but the match is case insensitive (uses regex, not glob).
  -inum n               File has inode number n. It is normally easier to use the -samefile test instead.
  -iregex pattern       Like -regex, but the match is case insensitive.
  -links n              File has n links.
  -lname pattern        File is a symbolic link whose contents match shell pattern.
  -mmin n               File's data was last modified n minutes ago.
  -mtime n              File's data was last modified n*24 hours ago.
  -name pattern         Base of file name (the path with the leading directories removed) matches shell pattern.
  -newer file           File was modified more recently than file.
  -path pattern         File name matches shell pattern.
  -perm mode            File's permission bits (no prefix, -, or /) (octal mode)
  -readable             Matches files which are readable.
  -regex pattern        File name matches regular expression pattern.
  -samefile name        File refers to the same inode as name.
  -size n               Note that if searching for files of size less than some value (e.g. -2k), must use equal sign (e.g. -size=-2k) so that the value is not interpreted incorrectly by argparse.
  -true                 Always true.
  -type c               File is of type c.
  -uid n                File's numeric user ID is n.
  -user uname           File is owned by user uname (numeric user ID allowed).
  -writable             Matches files which are writable.
  -fprint file          Output result to file.
  -ls                   List current file ls -dils format.
  -print                Print the full name on the standard output, followed by a newline, similar to GNU find.
  -print0               Print the full name on the standard output, followed by a null character, similar to GNU find.
  -printf format        Print format on the standard output, similar to GNU find.
  --num-results n       First n results.
  --smallest            Sort output by size, ascending.
  --largest             Sort output by size, descending.
  --compress            Try to reduce memory usage by compressing with zlib (if available).
  --delim c             Delimiter separating output columns
  --skip-file filename  Name of file containing directory basenames to skip
  -V, --verbose         Show the gufi_query being executed

Report bugs to the GitHub Issues page at https://github.com/mar-file-system/GUFI/issues
or by sending an email to <gufi-lanl@lanl.gov>

contents.text:
Use aggregate_sql_query when the answer must be correct across the whole index:
global totals, grouped totals, global ORDER BY/LIMIT, or top-N results.

Pipeline phases:
- I creates per-thread intermediate tables.
- E, S, and T read entries, summary, and treesummary data into intermediate.
- K creates the final aggregate table.
- J merges intermediate rows into aggregate.
- G returns final rows. Put global ORDER BY and LIMIT here.
- F is cleanup only; do not use it for final sorted output.

Critical rules:
- Do not put ORDER BY, LIMIT, or OFFSET in E, S, or T phases.
- Use K plus J plus G for index-wide sorted or top-N answers.
- Pass the index name from gufi://indexes unless intentionally querying an
  absolute index path.

Example: total regular-file bytes
- I: CREATE TABLE intermediate(size INT64)
- E: INSERT INTO intermediate SELECT size FROM vrpentries WHERE type = 'f'
- K: CREATE TABLE aggregate(total INT64)
- J: INSERT INTO aggregate SELECT SUM(size) FROM intermediate
- G: SELECT SUM(total) FROM aggregate

Example: top UIDs by regular-file bytes
- I: CREATE TABLE intermediate(uid INT64, total_bytes INT64)
- E: INSERT INTO intermediate SELECT uid, size FROM vrpentries WHERE type = 'f'
- K: CREATE TABLE aggregate(uid INT64, total_bytes INT64)
- J: INSERT INTO aggregate SELECT uid, SUM(total_bytes) FROM intermediate GROUP BY uid
- G: SELECT uid, total_bytes FROM aggregate ORDER BY total_bytes DESC LIMIT 10
